counterfactual_missing_items: Atypical endothelial cells, mitoses, or invasion (for angiosarcoma)
Hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, or dark coloration (for angiokeratoma)
Evidence of collateral circulation or underlying occlusion (for collateral vessel formation)
decisive_items: a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias
Discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels were observed, with superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels.
KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R identified as the only somatic mutation
response.rationale: C1 best integrates the clinical description of a solitary, blanchable telangiectatic plaque with histopath showing benign small-caliber vessels and a somatic KDR mutation, which together point to a solitary telangiectasia. R6 is the base diagnosis but lacks the solitary modifier. Other candidates are either unsupported (R1), rely solely on genetic finding without a clinical diagnosis (R2), or are contradicted by the blanchable, benign histology (R4, R5).

rejected.why: No raw support spans; the diagnosis is not directly evidenced by any vignette text.
The genetic finding alone does not define a clinical diagnosis; the lesion is still a telangiectasia, and the label is not a standard entity.
Angiosarcoma is contradicted by the blanchable nature, normal epidermis, and benign small-vessel lobules on histopathology.
Angiokeratoma is contradicted by the blanchable plaque and lack of hyperkeratosis or dark coloration.
